macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks were set for a cautious open as oil and geopolitical tensions eased
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. stock index futures edged higher as global markets and oil prices steadied after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran, with investors still watching geopolitical risks and energy prices closely. Bloomberg separately said Asian stocks were poised to fall after oil jumped on the Iran attack and a U.S. waiver for Iranian oil sales was revoked.

items.title: Fed officials signaled no immediate shift despite stronger growth data and jobs resilience
items.summary: Reuters said New York Fed President John Williams did not expect a sustained surge in energy prices, while broader market coverage noted investors were watching labor-market data and inflation signals for clues on the Fed path. MarketWatch also highlighted a jobs report showing June hiring of 57,000 and unemployment at 4.2%, with the report viewed as unlikely to change the Fed's stance quickly.

items.title: ECB meeting notes showed inflation still above target into next year
items.summary: Reuters reported that ECB policymakers were presented with projections showing inflation staying above target into next year despite nearly three rate hikes, reinforcing the view that policy easing may remain limited. The report suggested the ECB remains cautious about declaring victory over inflation.

items.title: Oil prices surged on Iran-related developments, raising inflation and market risks
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that oil climbed after the U.S. military launched fresh airstrikes in Iran and the Treasury revoked a waiver for Iranian oil sales, intensifying concern about supply disruption. Reuters also noted investors were weighing whether the conflict could stall broader de-escalation efforts.

items.title: China inflation data pointed to persistent producer-price pressure
items.summary: Reuters said China's producer prices surged for a fourth straight month to the highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also extended gains. The data pointed to continued cost pressure for domestic manufacturers.

items.title: PepsiCo beat quarterly revenue estimates
items.summary: Reuters reported that PepsiCo topped Wall Street estimates for second-quarter revenue, supported by improving demand for salty snacks in the U.S. and resilient demand for zero-sugar sodas. The company was cited as one of the notable corporate earnings stories of the day.

items.title: SK Hynix share offering drew strong demand
items.summary: Reuters reported that demand for SK Hynix's U.S. share offering was more than seven times the available shares. The strong order book highlighted continuing investor appetite for AI-linked semiconductor names.

items.title: U.S. labor-market data showed slower hiring but stable claims
items.summary: MarketWatch reported that the U.S. economy added 57,000 jobs in June and unemployment fell to 4.2%, while ADP data showed 98,000 private-sector jobs added and jobless claims remained low. Reuters said weekly claims fell, supporting the view that the labor market was still in a slow-hire, slow-fire mode.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI broadly releases GPT-5.6 and launches ChatGPT Work
items.summary: OpenAI has broadly released GPT-5.6 and introduced ChatGPT Work, an AI agent for gathering context across apps and files to create documents on Mac and Windows. The rollout also includes tiered pricing for GPT-5.6 variants.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agentic tasks. The release adds another major frontier-model update in a fast-moving market.

items.title: Meta plans to start manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is reportedly preparing to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip in September, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. The move is part of a broader plan to raise its computing power to 14 gigawatts next year.

items.title: UN digital tech agency launches initiative to improve trust in AI agents
items.summary: The UN's digital technology agency announced a new initiative to improve trust in AI agents as concerns grow about accountability and human oversight in increasingly autonomous systems. The effort reflects rising regulatory and governance attention on agentic AI.

items.title: Saudi Arabia's Humain and Cohere deepen AI compute and sovereign model partnership
items.summary: Humain and Cohere said they will collaborate on AI compute and sovereign AI models, expanding international AI infrastructure ties in the Gulf. The announcement underscores continued investment in regional AI capacity.

items.title: OpenAI copyright dispute escalates with New York Times sanctions motion
items.summary: News publishers including the New York Times say OpenAI hid tools and datasets that could identify copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs, escalating the litigation with a new motion for sanctions. The dispute highlights ongoing legal pressure around training data and output provenance.

items.title: Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
items.summary: Google is changing ad transparency by disclosing which ads were made with AI. The move signals a broader industry trend toward labeling synthetic media and AI-assisted marketing content.

items.title: AI-generated viruses raise biosafety concerns after research breakthrough
items.summary: CNN reports on scientists using an AI model to create 16 new viruses capable of infecting bacteria, a development that has prompted concern about potential misuse. The result highlights both the power and the biosafety risks of AI-assisted biological design.
